Following up from last week's pipeline review. NimbleApps is moving the pilot 6–8 weeks earlier if we can guarantee a short burst of dedicated capacity for their PoC (more live tokens, live-eval load). I uploaded a quick runway sheet (attached) that maps the current close projections to reserve/ondemand needs.

Quick asks for today's stand:

- Karthik & Laura: finance-facing numbers for commit vs burst cost delta (we need a one-page slide for Sales).

Logan —

Quick feasibility check: technically we can spin a 2-week +60 GPU burst, but there are two caveats: (1) provisioning lead time for the specific A100/80GB footprints we use for Nimble's model variants is ~10 business days for dedicated rack allocation, (2) we need a mandatory cooldown window after the burst to defragment KV cache and re-balance other reserved pools.

Operational impact:
- Locking 60 GPUs for 2 weeks will reduce available burst capacity for other pilots — I recommend a conservative safety margin (keep 12 GPUs uncommitted).
- We can offer an automated fall-back to a quantized variant (x4 cheaper) if live latency SLOs slip under sustained load.

I'll attach a short ops checklist to this thread by 12:00 PT and flag any parts that require infra lead-time. Marissa: can you confirm whether the 10-business-day estimate works if we start engraving now?

Ben

Logan / Finance & Sales —

I ran a baseline comparison using the sheet. Two scenarios for the customer ask (2-week, +60 GPUs starting 2027-07-05):

Scenario A — Reserve top-up (short-term commit):
- 60 GPUs reserved for 2 weeks: estimated cost delta vs current commit = $72,000 (one-off amortized over quarter).
- Benefit: guaranteed throughput, no dynamic throttling; simpler SLA.

Scenario B — On-demand burst with fallback to quantized model:
- Expected spend = $46,500 for the 2-week window + potential penalty for preemption risk.
- Benefit: lower nominal cost, requires acceptance of degraded latency in tail cases.

Action for Sales slide: two line-items (Reserve vs Burst) with trade-offs. Laura — can you draft the slide copy? Also attaching a short cost calc screenshot.

Quick ops note —

Ben is correct on the 10 business-day lead time for A100 racks if we want physical isolation. If Nimble will accept a mixed pool (some shared racks + reserved slices) we can reduce lead time to ~4 business days by using pre-warm node snapshots and KV cache priming. Steps I recommend:

1) Approve mixed-mode: reserve 40 GPUs (dedicated) + 20 GPUs as pre-warmed shared nodes.
2) Pre-warm 20 nodes with Nimble model weights and launch cache seeding 72 hours before go-live.
3) Post-burst cooldown: 48 hours for cache reconciliation and rebalancing; schedule maintenance window.

Attachments: ops_checklist.txt (stub) — contains node snapshot checklist, cache-seed command, and rollback playbook.

Marissa Cole
